chunks: And Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār narrated, saying:

I said to Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام: A man has money with another man, so he gives it to him as a loan, and it remains with the man for a long time, with no benefit from it reaching its owner. Then the man gives him something after something, disliking that he should take back his money where he gets no benefit from it. Is that permissible for him? He said: There is no harm, if the two of them did not stipulate it.

key_terms.شَرَطَاهُ: made it a stipulated condition between them
key_terms.قَرْضًا: a loan given to another person
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is permitted
key_terms.مَنْفَعَةٌ: a benefit or gain derived from the loan arrangement

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a borrower to give gifts to a lender if no condition was stipulated in the loan?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a lender receiving occasional gifts from a borrower. It indicates that such a benefit is permissible so long as it was not made a condition of the loan, which distinguishes lawful courtesy from usury.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
I said to Abu Ibrahim (Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim (as)): "A man has some money with another man as a loan, and it remains with him for a long time without providing any benefit to the owner. So the borrower occasionally gives the lender something out of courtesy, to avoid returning the money without any benefit. Is this permissible for him?"
Imam (as) said: "There is no harm, as long as they did not stipulate it as a condition."
